en.title: Index of the First Non-Positive Prefix Sum
en.description:
Find the earliest non-empty prefix whose sum is ≤0; if there is none, output −1. This site's standard I/O explicitly uses 0-based indices: the source's examples 2 and 3 mix index conventions, so the result of example 2 is corrected from 2 to 1.

The standard I/O and the solution were written independently by this site; ranges marked as this site's are not the original source constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n (1..100000), and the second line contains n integers in −10^9..10^9.
en.explanation: Example 1: the prefixes 1 and 3 are both positive, so output −1. Example 2: the prefixes are 2, −2, −1, and the first one occurs at index 1. Example 3: the prefixes are 1, 3, 6, 0, and the first one is at index 3.
hints: Accumulate the prefix sum and, as soon as it is ≤0, return the current 0-based index.
